title: Bell Stair
shortDescription: A tight oak stair turns down from the empty bell frame.
longDescription:
The stair leaves the Clock Tower in a tight coil. Oak steps are polished by older feet than yours. Fine silk has caught on the newel and shakes when the gears above turn.
The humming is louder here. It is not a swinging bell. Something below is answering the wood.

fixtures.name: Stairkeeper Vane
fixtures.lookDescription: A hedgehog sits on the fourth step with a lamp-trimming kit open beside her. Try talk vane.
fixtures.examineDescription: A hedgehog in a canvas apron with a lamp-trimming kit open on the step beside her: wick shears, a tin of oil, a rag gone black. She keeps the stair lamps lit, which is the job Keeper Holm had before her, and she took it on knowing that. Her quills are singed short along one shoulder. She does not go below the cloister and does not pretend the reason is a rule.
fixtures.dialogue: Vane trims a wick to length before she looks up, because the wick is on fire and you are not. "Somebody has to keep this stair lit. Holm did. Now I do, and I do it from up here, which I will not dress up as bravery." She snuffs the taper. "There is a thing in the cloister I want carried up into lamplight where I can look at it. Talk vane."

fixtures.name: Stair Rope
fixtures.examineDescription: The hand-rope is hemp over living oak. Three slow pulses travel up the grain — the same count you felt in the empty frame. Fresh silk has caught on the newel. That silk was not here when the bell still hung. Alder will want this named, not guessed.
